titulo: Unit 7: Databases & Passive Voice (RA1, RA2, RA3, RA5)

paginas.contenido:
This unit covers several Learning Outcomes (RA) essential for your technical profile in ASIR.
  • RA1 & RA2: Understanding technical documentation and reading comprehension in IT environments.
  • RA3: Effective communication in professional and social settings (Interviews).
  • RA5: Mastering complex grammatical structures (Passive Voice & Causatives) to write objective reports.

💡 Nota: Esta lección integra los resultados de aprendizaje RA1, RA2, RA3 y RA5, enfocándose en bases de datos y gramática avanzada.

Every computer user must master office applications (spreadsheets, presentations, databases) to organize information efficiently.

Key Concepts:

  • DBMS (Database Management System): Specialized software used to handle large and complex databases.
  • DBA (Database Administrator): The IT specialist responsible for organizing and protecting data.
  • MySQL: A popular open-source DBMS known for its stability and web compatibility.

💡 Nota: Un DBA es la persona, mientras que el DBMS es el software (ej. MySQL).

Mastering these terms is vital for managing SQL tables and data structures.
TermDefinition
TableThe basic structure used to organize data into rows and columns.
RecordA complete set of fields describing one item (a row).
FieldA single category of information (a column).
Primary KeyA unique value for each record (no duplicates).
CellThe intersection of a row and a column.
TypeThe kind of data a field can contain (text, number, date).

The Passive Voice shifts focus from the doer to the action or the recipient.
  • Structure: Subject + Be + Past Participle.
  • Formal Tone: Essential for incident reports and technical audits.
  • "Get" Passive: More informal, often used for unexpected events ("The server got hacked").

💡 Nota: Usamos la pasiva cuando el 'quién' lo hizo no es importante o se quiere ser más objetivo.

Observe how the verb 'to be' changes according to the timeframe.
TenseActivePassive
Present SimpleI process backups.Backups are processed.
Past SimpleI tested the code.The code was tested.
Future SimpleI will install software.Software will be installed.
Present PerfectI have sent the logs.Logs have been sent.
ModalsI should check logs.Logs should be checked.

Causatives indicate that one person causes another to do something.
  • LET: To permit/allow. "My boss lets me work from home."
  • MAKE: To force/pressure. "The admin made us change passwords."
  • GET: To convince/request (indirect). "I got them to fix the router."
  • HAVE: To convince/encourage. "I'll have the technician sign the report."
  • HELP: To aid someone. "I helped him to update the server."

💡 Nota: El causativo 'Have something done' es muy común en servicios externos (ej. 'Have my car repaired').

Technical support often involves human interaction where clarity is key.

Dialogue Key Terms:

  • Appointment: Citación o cita programada.
  • Symptoms: Indicadores de un problema (médico o técnico).
  • Medication / Treatment: Solución aplicada para corregir el estado.
  • Pharmacist: El especialista que provee la solución.

💡 Nota: En IT usamos 'Troubleshooting' de forma similar a un diagnóstico médico.

Preparing for a technical interview is part of RA3. Master these common questions:
  • "Can you describe your experience with DBMS?" (Use specific names like MySQL).
  • "How do you handle data security?" (Talk about backups and primary keys).
  • "Describe a situation where you had to lead a project." (Use clear, structured English).

Review these core concepts for Unit 7 (RA1, 2, 3, 5).
  • DB Basics: Tables store records (rows) and fields (columns). PKs are unique.
  • Passive: Focuses on the system action. Essential for professional reports.
  • Causatives: Used to delegate or allow actions (Let, Make, Get, Have).
  • Roles: DBAs manage the DBMS to ensure data integrity and security.
Complete this test to confirm you have mastered the Unit 7 content.

preguntas_test.q: Data backups ___ by the server every night. (Present Passive)
preguntas_test.explicacion: Como 'Backups' es plural, usamos 'are' + el participio 'processed'.

preguntas_test.q: The new software ___ by the IT team next week.
preguntas_test.explicacion: Para el futuro en pasiva usamos 'will be' + participio.

preguntas_test.q: What is a 'DBA' in an IT context?
preguntas_test.explicacion: DBA son las siglas de Database Administrator, el responsable de gestionar los datos.
preguntas_test.ejemplo: Ej: 'The DBA recovered the database after the crash.'

preguntas_test.q: Which database term refers to a vertical group of cells (a column)?
preguntas_test.explicacion: En bases de datos, 'Field' (campo) representa una columna de información específica.

preguntas_test.q: The virus ___ from the network yesterday.
preguntas_test.explicacion: Usamos el pasado simple en pasiva ('was' + participio) por la marca temporal 'yesterday'.

preguntas_test.q: Causative: 'I am going ________ at the new hairdresser's.'
preguntas_test.explicacion: Usamos la estructura causative 'get/have + object + past participle' cuando alguien hace algo por nosotros.
preguntas_test.ejemplo: Ej: 'I need to get my laptop fixed.'

preguntas_test.q: Which verb means to force or pressure someone to do something?
preguntas_test.explicacion: 'Make' se usa en causativa para indicar obligación o presión.
preguntas_test.ejemplo: Ej: 'The policy makes all users change passwords.'

preguntas_test.q: What is the intersection of a row and a column in a table?
preguntas_test.explicacion: Una celda ('Cell') es el punto exacto donde se cruzan una fila y una columna.
preguntas_test.ejemplo: Ej: 'Click on the cell to edit the value.'

preguntas_test.q: Relative Pronouns: 'The server, ___ was upgraded, is down again.'
preguntas_test.explicacion: Usamos 'which' para referirnos a objetos (el servidor).
preguntas_test.ejemplo: Ej: 'The app which I downloaded is buggy.'

preguntas_test.q: Which causative verb means 'to allow or permit'?
preguntas_test.ejemplo: Ej: 'The admin lets us access the server room.'
